In this case, we use the double-angle formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Rearranging the above formula, we get

$$
\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (2x-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)\text{d}x \\  & =2(\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2})-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+C \\  & ={x}^{2}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
